why_them: We cite them eight times across Como and Florence; an Italian project that writes about monumental trees province by province, which is what our city pages are.
Cited five times on Prague trees; a Prague conservation group, and Prague is 17 published trees.
Cited on Bucaco, Palermo and Sardinia; measuring giant trees is their whole subject and ours overlaps exactly.
Cited four times on Paris trees, and it is a named person rather than a general inbox, which is the kind that answers.
Cited four times on London trees; a city-discovery blog, the same shape as Lisboa Secreta.

Cited on Aarhus and Copenhagen. A general inbox at a big national body, so the measured odds are worse than for the others here; worth one mail because Denmark is 23 trees and the Dendrology Society thread is already warm.

Named to us by Giulia Torta, who runs the Orto botanico di Firenze: they promote Florence's monumental trees, run tree walks with the garden, and publish a downloadable map of every monumental tree in the city. A referral, so the mail opens with her name. They also hold photographs, which their site does not licence, so that is a permission ask rather than a download.
